findings.F1: The check failed on Calmar alone (0.568 against 0.75). A yearly return of +14.5 % meets a deepest fall of 25.6 %, built over 48 days from window w1 into w2 while the coins fell 59.5 %. In w2 the 73 active weekend-fall cases lost against the coin's drift (mean excess 3-day return −5.12 %, t −3.17), and in w17 the 30 cases did the same (−7.54 %, t −3.31). The other falls were 13.8 % (w17–w18), 11.7 % (w15–w16) and 10.5 % (w11–w13).
findings.F2: The rebound comes almost entirely from Sundays that close below the coin's 50-day average. Those 703 cases have a mean excess of +1.56 % (t 4.46) and summed position gains of 12.9; the 96 cases above the average have +0.14 % (t 0.14) and 0.47. A case-book of the below-average cases falls at most 5.1 % against 17.1 % for all cases, a gain-to-fall ratio of 18.0 against 8.6, though the 628 cases too early in their window for a 50-day average drop out of that comparison. The condition alone does not earn: Sundays below the average without the signal have −1.35 % (t −5.05, 827 cases). It belongs to the theory because a weekend sell-off in a coin already under pressure is the one-sided flow a thin book overprices.
findings.F3: The size of the weekend fall against the coin's usual daily move grades the rebound strongly, with the Sunday return divided by the 60-day daily standard deviation. The quartile of largest falls returns +3.30 % excess (t 4.79, 172 cases), against +2.20 %, +0.72 % and +0.04 % for the other quartiles. The raw Sunday-return quartiles show the same, from +2.97 % (t 4.46) to −0.06 %. Cases beyond one usual move (145) give +3.29 % (t 4.32), and their case-book falls at most 3.7 %. Sundays with such a fall but no signal earn −1.02 % (t −0.59, 70 cases), so the measure is not an effect of its own.
findings.F4: The rebound is larger when the coin's last 20 days were turbulent against its last 60. The top quartile of the 20-day/60-day volatility ratio gives +3.33 % excess (t 5.86) and the bottom quartile +0.57 % (t 0.67). The same quartiles on Sundays without the signal earn −0.30 % (t −0.69) and −1.56 % (t −4.14), so turbulence alone does not earn. Cases above the median ratio cut the case-book's deepest fall from 17.1 % to 4.8 %, with the same gain-to-fall ratio (8.6). The 20-day volatility level grades the same way, from +0.32 % (t 0.62) to +4.03 % (t 5.37).
findings.F5: The 20-day decline already grades the rebound inside the active cases, but it does not keep the book out of crashes. The quartile with the deepest 20-day fall gives +3.38 % (t 5.14) against +0.88 % (t 1.54) for the shallowest. The worst falls nonetheless come from broad sell-offs. The worst single Sunday had 12 coins active at once, a mean excess of −30.4 % and a summed position loss of 2.82. The worst-decile Sundays carried larger positions (mean allocation 0.71 against 0.55).
findings.F6: The move per case is far above the cost of a trade, so cost is not why the book fails. The total move is +1.98 %, 8.9 times the 0.22 % cost, and the unusual move is +1.50 %, a strength of 0.17. The book fails on its falls, not on its gain: Sharpe 0.88, 0.27 above holding, with no window decisive (lowest leave-one-out Sharpe 0.78).

ideas.idea: A coin that fell over the weekend (its Saturday-to-Sunday close-to-close return) rises over the next 3 days (Monday to Wednesday), the larger the weekend fall, the larger the rise, and the rise is larger the further its Sunday close sits below its 50-day average price.
ideas.consequence: Buy weekend falls in coins trading under their 50-day average, more the further below, and refuse those in coins above it, which avoids the trades that carry the book's falls without the rebound.
ideas.name: weekend fall below average

ideas.idea: A coin that fell over the weekend (its Saturday-to-Sunday close-to-close return) rises over the next 3 days (Monday to Wednesday), and the rise is larger the larger that fall is measured in units of the coin's usual daily move over its past 60 days.
ideas.consequence: Size weekend-fall buys by how unusual the fall is for that coin, so small routine dips get little capital and the book's losses on them shrink.
ideas.name: weekend fall in vol units

ideas.idea: A coin that fell over the weekend (its Saturday-to-Sunday close-to-close return) rises over the next 3 days (Monday to Wednesday), the larger the weekend fall, the larger the rise, and the rise is larger the higher the coin's 20-day volatility stands against its 60-day volatility.
ideas.consequence: Favour weekend-fall buys when the coin has turned turbulent, and keep them small in calm stretches where the rebound barely shows.
ideas.name: weekend fall in turbulence
